reference_sql:
WITH order_units AS (
  SELECT order_id, SUM(quantity) AS units
  FROM order_lines
  GROUP BY order_id
)
SELECT o.customer_id, COUNT(*) AS n_orders, COALESCE(SUM(u.units), 0) AS units
FROM orders o
LEFT JOIN order_units u ON u.order_id = o.order_id
WHERE o.customer_id BETWEEN 1001 AND 1500
GROUP BY o.customer_id
alternatives: SELECT o.customer_id, COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS n_orders, COALESCE(SUM(ol.quantity), 0) AS units FROM orders o LEFT JOIN order_lines ol ON ol.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.customer_id BETWEEN 1001 AND 1500 GROUP BY o.customer_id

WITH order_units AS (SELECT order_id, SUM(quantity) AS units FROM order_lines GROUP BY order_id) SELECT o.customer_id, COUNT(o.order_id) AS n_orders, SUM(COALESCE(u.units, 0)) AS units FROM order_units u RIGHT JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = u.order_id WHERE o.customer_id >= 1001 AND o.customer_id <= 1500 GROUP BY o.customer_id

other_way.sql: SELECT o.customer_id, COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS n_orders, COALESCE(SUM(ol.quantity), 0) AS units FROM orders o LEFT JOIN order_lines ol ON ol.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.customer_id BETWEEN 1001 AND 1500 GROUP BY o.customer_id
other_way.tradeoff: Counting different order IDs after joining the lines is shorter, but only the per-order step keeps every later sum safe.
